title: Primes in sequences and gaps
summary: Which sequences contain infinitely many primes, how large gaps between consecutive primes can be, and how often primes fall in short intervals. Most such questions are open; sieves and the circle method give the partial results.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #141
research_problems.statement: Let $k≥3$. Are there $k$ consecutive primes in arithmetic progression?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #860
research_problems.statement:
Let $h(n)$ be such that, for any $m\geq 1$, in the interval $(m,m+h(n))$ there exist distinct
integers $a_i$ for $1\leq i\leq \pi(n)$ such that $p_i\mid a_i$, where $p_i$ denotes the $i$th
prime.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #997
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that, for every $\alpha$, the sequence $\{ \alpha p_n\}$ is not well-distributed,
if $p_n$ is the sequence of primes?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #427
research_problems.statement:
is it true that, for every $n$ and $d$, there exists $k$ such that
$$
  d \mid p_{n + 1} + \cdots + p_{n + k},
$$
where $p_r$ denotes the $r$th prime?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1212
research_problems.statement:
Let $G$ be the graph with vertex set those pairs $(x,y)\in \mathbb{N}^2$ with
$\mathrm{gcd}(x,y)=1$, in which we join two vertices if the differ in only one coordinate, and
there by $\pm 1$.

Is there a path going to infinity on $G$, say $P$, such that for all $(x,y)\in P$ both
$\min(x,y)>1$ and at least one of $x$ or $y$ is composite?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #431
research_problems.statement:
Are there two infinite sets $A$ and $B$ such that $A+B$ agrees with the primes up to finitely
many exceptions?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #233
research_problems.statement:
A conjecture by Heath-Brown:
The sum of squares of the first $N$ gaps between consecutive primes behaves like $N * (log N)^2$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #850
research_problems.statement:
Can there exist two distinct integers $x$ and $y$ such that $x,y$ have the same prime factors,
$x+1,y+1$ have the same prime factors, and $x+2,y+2$ also have the same prime factors?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #9
research_problems.statement:
Is the upper density of the set of odd numbers that cannot be expressed as a prime plus
two powers of 2 positive?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #10
research_problems.statement:
Is there some $k$ such that every large integer is the sum of a prime and at most $k$
powers of $2$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #203
research_problems.statement:
Is there an integer $m$ with $(m, 6) = 1$ such that none of $2^k \cdot 3^\ell \cdot m + 1$ are prime,
for any $k, \ell \ge 0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1187
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $k\geq 3$. Is it true that, in any finite colouring of the integers, there are monochromatic
arithmetic progressions of primes of length $k$?

(b) Let $k\geq 3$. In any finite colouring of the integers, are there monochromatic arithmetic
progressions of length $k$ whose common difference is a prime?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #852
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $h(x)$ be maximal such that for
some $n < x$ the numbers $d_n, d_{n+1}, \ldots, d_{n+h(x)-1}$ are all distinct [Er85c]. Estimate
$h(x)$. In particular, is it true that
$$h(x) > (\log x)^c$$
for some constant $c > 0$?

(b) Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $h(x)$ be maximal such that for
some $n < x$ the numbers $d_n, d_{n+1}, \ldots, d_{n+h(x)-1}$ are all distinct [Er85c]. Estimate
$h(x)$. In particular, is it true that
$$h(x) = o(\log x)?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #461
research_problems.statement:
Let $s_t(n)$ be the $t$-smooth component of $n$ - that is, the product of all primes $p$ (with
multiplicity) dividing $n$ such that $p<t$. Let $f(n,t)$ count the number of distinct possible
values for $s_t(m)$ for $m\in [n+1,n+t]$. Is it true that
$$f(n,t)\gg t$$
(uniformly, for all $t$ and $n$)?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #454
research_problems.statement: Is it true that `limsup (fun n => (f n - 2 * n.nth Prime : ℕ∞)) atTop = ⊤`?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #244
research_problems.statement:
Let $C > 1$. Does the set of integers of the form $p + \lfloor C^k \rfloor$,
for some prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$, have density $>0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1059
research_problems.statement: Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p - k!$ is composite for each $k$ such that $1 ≤ k! < p$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #890
research_problems.statement:
(a) If $\omega_k(n)$ counts the number of distinct prime factors of $n$ which are $>k$, then is it true
that, for every $k\geq 1$,
$$\liminf_{n\to \infty}\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega_k(n+i)\leq k?$$

(b) Is it true that
$$\limsup_{n\to \infty}\left(\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega(n+i)\right) \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}=1,$$
where $\omega$ counts the number of distinct prime factors without restriction?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #463
research_problems.statement:
Is there a function $f$ with $f(n)\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ such that,
for all large $n$, there is a composite number $m$ such that
$$
n + f(n) < m < n + p(m)
$$
Here $p(m)$ is the least prime factor of $m$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #428
research_problems.statement:
Is there a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that, for infinitely many $n$, all of $n-a$
are prime for all $a\in A$ with $0 < a < n$ and $$\liminf\frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{\pi(x)}>0?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #5
research_problems.statement:
Let $C\geq 0$. Is there an infinite sequence of $n_i$ such that
$$\lim_{i\to \infty}\frac{p_{n_i+1}-p_{n_i}}{\log n_i}=C?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #682
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that for almost all $n$ there exists some $m\in (p_n,p_{n+1})$ such that
$$p(m) \geq p_{n+1}-p_n,$$
where $p(m)$ denotes the least prime factor of $m$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #236
research_problems.statement: Let $f(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n=p+2^k$ for prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$. Show that $f(n)=o(\log n)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1139
research_problems.statement:
Let $1\leq u_1 < u_2 < \cdots$ be the sequence of integers with at most $2$ prime factors.
Is it true that $$\limsup_{k \to \infty} \frac{u_{k+1}-u_k}{\log k}=\infty?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #950
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(n) = \sum_{p<n}\frac{1}{n-p}$.

(a) Is it true that $\liminf f(n)=1$?

(b) Is it true that $\limsup f(n)=\infty$?

(c) Is it true that $f(n)=o(\log\log n)$ for all $n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #462
research_problems.statement:
Let $p(n)$ denote the least prime factor of $n$. Is there a constant $C>0$ such that
$$\sum_{x\leq n\leq x+C\sqrt{x}(\log x)^2}\frac{p(n)}{n}\gg 1$$
for all sufficiently large $x$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #16
research_problems.statement:
Is the set of odd integers not of the form $2^k+p$ the union of an infinite arithmetic progression
and a set of density $0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #459
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(u)$ be the largest $v$ such that no $m\in (u,v)$ is composed entirely of primes dividing
$uv$. Estimate $f(u)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1141
research_problems.statement: Are there infinitely many $n$ such that $n-k^2$ is prime for all $k$ with $(n,k)=1$ and $k^2 < n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #238
research_problems.statement:
Let `c₁, c₂ > 0`. Is it true that for any sufficiently large `x`, there exists more than
`c₁ * log x` many consecutive primes `≤ x` such that the difference between any two is `> c₂`?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1055
research_problems.statement:
A prime $p$ is in class $1$ if the only prime divisors of $p+1$ are
$2$ or $3$. In general, a prime $p$ is in class $r$ if every prime factor
of $p+1$ is in some class $\leq r-1$, with equality for at least one prime factor.
Are there infinitely many primes in each class?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #358
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $A=\{a_1 < \cdots\}$ be an infinite sequence of integers. Let $f(n)$ count the number of
solutions to $$n=\sum_{u\leq i\leq v}a_i.$$
Is there such an $A$ for which $f(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$?

(b) Let $A=\{a_1 < \cdots\}$ be an infinite sequence of integers. Let $f(n)$ count the number of
solutions to $$n=\sum_{u\leq i\leq v}a_i.$$
Is there an $A$ such that $f(n)\geq 2$ for all large $n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #681
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that for all large $n$ there exists $k$
such that $n + k$ is composite and $p(n+k) > k^2$,
where $p(m)$ is the least prime factor of $m$ ?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1138
research_problems.statement:
Given a pair $(x,y)$, this is the amount of primes in the interval above $y$, of length
equalling the largest prime gap before $x$, scaled by a constant $C$.

**Erdős Problem 1138.**
Let $x/2 < y < x$ and $C > 1$. If $d = \max_{p_n < x}(p_{n+1} - p_n)$,
where $p_n$ denotes the $n$-th prime, then is it true that
$$\pi(y + Cd) - \pi(y) \sim \frac{Cd}{\log y}$$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #375
research_problems.statement: Is `Erdos375Prop` true?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #458
research_problems.statement:
Let $\operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, n)$ denote the least common multiple of $\{1, \dots, n\}$.
Let $p_k$ be the $k$-th prime.
Is it true that for all $k \geq 1$, $\operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, p_{k+1}-1) < p_k \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, p_k)$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #4
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that, for any $C > 0$, there infinitely many $n$ such that:
$$
  p_{n + 1} - p_n > C \frac{\log\log n\log\log\log\log n}{(\log\log\log n) ^ 2}\log n
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #49
research_problems.statement:
Let $A=\{a_1<\cdots<a_t\}\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be such that $\phi(a_1)<\cdots<\phi(a_t)$.
The primes are such an example. Are they the largest possible? Can one show that
$\lvert A\rvert<(1+o(1))\pi(N)$ or even $\lvert A\rvert=o(N)$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #17
research_problems.statement: Are there infinitely many cluster primes?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #853
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $r(x)$ be the smallest even
integer $t$ such that $d_n = t$ has no solutions for $n \le x$.

Is it true that $r(x) \to \infty$?

(b) Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $r(x)$ be the smallest even
integer $t$ such that $d_n = t$ has no solutions for $n \le x$.

Is it true that $r(x) / \log x \to \infty$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #683
research_problems.statement:
Let $P(n, k)$ be the largest prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$.

Let $P(n, k)$ be the largest prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$.
There exists $c > 0$ such that $P(n, k) \ge \min(n - k + 1, k^{1 + c})$ for all $0 < k \le n/2$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1202
research_problems.statement:
Let $\epsilon > 0$. Does there exist $k$ such that, for every $n$, any primes
$p_1 < \cdots < p_k < n^{1-\epsilon}$ and any sets $A_i$ of $\frac{p_i - 1}{2}$ residue classes
modulo $p_i$, the number of $m \le n$ that avoid $A_i \pmod{p_i}$ for every $i$ is at most
$\epsilon n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #6
research_problems.statement:
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n < d_{n+1} < d_{n+2}$, where $d$
denotes the prime gap function.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1142
research_problems.statement: Are there infinitely many $n > 2$ such that $n - 2^k$ is prime for all $k \geq 1$ with $2^k < n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #234
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that for all `c ≥ 0`, the density `f c` of integers for which
`(p (n + 1) - p n) / log n < c` exists and is a continuous function of `c`?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #855
research_problems.statement:
Erdős Problem 855 (Segal's conjecture): $\pi(x + y) \le \pi(x) + \pi(y)$
for all sufficiently large $x, y$, i.e. for all $x, y \ge N$ for some $N$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1201
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that for every $\epsilon,\eta>0$ there exists a $k$ such that the density of $n$
for which $P(n(n+1)\cdots(n+k))>n^{1-\epsilon}$ is at least $1-\eta$ (where $P(m)$ is the greatest
prime divisor of $m$)?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #680
research_problems.statement:
(a) Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $n$, there exists some $k$ such that
$$
p(n+k)>k^2+1,
$$
where $p(m)$ denotes the least prime factor of $m$?

(b) Can one prove this is false if we replace $k^2+1$ by $e^{(1+\epsilon)\sqrt{k}}+C_\epsilon$, for all
$\epsilon>0$, where $C_\epsilon>0$ is some constant?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #685
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $\epsilon > 0$ and let $n$ be large depending on $\epsilon$. Is it true that for all
$n^{\epsilon} < k \leq n^{1-\epsilon}$ the number of distinct prime divisors of $\binom{n}{k}$ is
$$(1+o(1))\, k \sum_{k < p < n} \frac{1}{p}?$$

(b) Is it true that, for some constant $c > 0$, the number of distinct prime divisors of
$\binom{n}{k}$ is
$$(1+o(1))\, k \sum_{k < p < n} \frac{1}{p}$$
even for all $(\log n)^c \leq k \leq n^{1-\epsilon}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #219
research_problems.statement:
Are there arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions of primes?
Solution: yes.
Ref: Green, Ben and Tao, Terence, _The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions_

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1137
research_problems.statement:
Let $d_n=p_{n+1}-p_n$, where $p_n$ denotes the $n$th prime. Is it true that
$$\frac{\max_{n < x}d_{n}d_{n-1}}{(\max_{n < x}d_n)^2}\to 0$$ as $x\to \infty$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #200
research_problems.statement: Does the longest arithmetic progression of primes in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ have length $o(\log N)$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #279
research_problems.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$. Is there a choice of congruence classes $a_p\pmod{p}$ for every prime $p$
such that all sufficiently large integers can be written as $a_p+tp$ for some prime $p$
and integer $t\geq k$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #15
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that $\sum_{n=1}^\infty(-1)^n\frac{n}{p_n}$ converges,
where $p_n$ is the sequence of primes?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #237
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be a set such that $\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg \log N$ for
all large $N$. Let $f(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n=p+a$ for $p$ prime and $a\in A$. Is
it true that $\limsup f(n)=\infty$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 32
research_problems.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $A \subset \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ be a set of size $\lfloor \sqrt{p} \rfloor$.
Is there a dilate of $A$ containing a gap of length $100\sqrt{p}$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 44
research_problems.statement:
Sieve $[N]$ by removing half the residue classes mod $p_i$, for primes
$2 \leqslant p_1 < p_2 < \dots < p_{1000} < N^{9/10}$. Does the remaining set have size at most
$\frac{1}{10} N$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 45
research_problems.statement:
Can we pick residue classes $a_p \pmod{p}$, one for each prime $p \leq N$, such that every
integer $\leq N$ lies in at least $10$ of them?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 46
research_problems.statement:
Given $x$ and $y$, can we cover the interval $[1, y]$ by residue classes $a_p \pmod p$
for each prime $p \le x$?

We conjecture that the best-known lower bound can be improved.

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 62
research_problems.statement:
Let $p$ be a large prime, and let $A$ be the set of all primes less than $p$.
Is every $x \in \{1, \ldots, p-1\}$ congruent to some product $a_1 a_2$ where $a_1, a_2 \in A$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 64
research_problems.statement:
Do there exist infinitely many primes $p$ for which $p - 2$ has an odd number of prime factors,
counted with multiplicity (i.e. $\Omega(p - 2)$ is odd)?

title: Smooth, powerful and squarefree numbers
summary: $n$ is $y$-smooth if all its prime factors are $\le y$, powerful if $p\mid n \Rightarrow p^2 \mid n$, squarefree if no $p^2$ divides it. Their counts are governed by Dickman's function, $\zeta(3/2)/\zeta(3)\cdot\sqrt x$ and $6x/\pi^2$.

prerequisites.title: Primes and the fundamental theorem of arithmetic

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #366
research_problems.statement: Are there any $2$-full $n$ such that $n+1$ is $3$-full?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #323
research_problems.statement:
Let $1\leq m\leq k$ and $f_{k,m}(x)$ denote the number of integers $\leq x$ which are the sum of
$m$ many nonnegative $k$th powers.

(a) Is it true that $f_{k,k}(x) \gg_\epsilon x^{1-\epsilon}$ for all $\epsilon>0$?

(b) Is it true that if $m < k$ then $f_{k,m}(x) \gg x^{m/k}$ for sufficiently large $x$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #937
research_problems.statement:
Are there infinitely many four-term arithmetic progressions of coprime powerful numbers?
(A number $n$ is *powerful* if $p \mid n \to p^2 \mid n$; `Nat.Powerful`.)

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #324
research_problems.statement:
Does there exist a polynomial $f(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that all the sums $f(a)+f(b)$ with
$a < b$ nonnegative integers are distinct?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #942
research_problems.statement:
Let $h(n)$ count the number of powerful integers in $[n^2, (n + 1)^2)$.

Is there some constant $c > 0$ such that $h(n) < (\log n)^{c + o(1)}$ and, for infinitely many $n$,
$h(n) > (\log n)^{c - o(1)}$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #365
research_problems.statement:
(a) Do all pairs of consecutive powerful numbers $n$ and $n+1$ come from solutions to Pell
equations? In other words, must either $n$ or $n+1$ be a square?

(b) Is the number of positive $n\leq x$ such that $n$ and $n+1$ are both powerful bounded
by $(\log x)^{O(1)}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #943
research_problems.statement: Let $A$ be the set of powerful numbers. Is is true that $1_A\ast 1_A(n)=n^{o(1)}$ for every $n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #773
research_problems.statement: What is the size of the largest Sidon subset $A\subseteq\{1,2^2,\ldots,N^2\}$? Is it $N^{1-o(1)}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #367
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $B_2(n)$ be the $2$-full part of $n$ (that is, $B_2(n)=n/n'$ where $n'$ is the product of all
primes that divide $n$ exactly once). Is it true that, for every fixed $k \geq 1$,
$\prod_{n \leq m < n+k} B_2(m) \ll n^{2+o(1)}$?

(b) Or perhaps even $\prod_{n \leq m < n+k} B_2(m) \ll_k n^2$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #888
research_problems.statement:
What is the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that if
$a\leq b\leq c\leq d\in A$ are such that $abcd$ is a square then $ad=bc$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #325
research_problems.statement:
Writing $f_{k, 3}(x)$ for the number of integers $\leq x$ which are the sum of three $k$th powers,
is it true that $f_{k, 3}(x) \gg x ^ (3 / k)$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #939
research_problems.statement: If $r≥4$ then can the sum of $r-2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers ever be itself $r$-powerful?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #938
research_problems.statement:
Let $A=\{n_1 < n_2 < \cdots\}$ be the sequence of powerful numbers (if $p\mid n$ then $p^2\mid n$).
Are there only finitely many three-term progressions of consecutive terms $n_k,n_{k+1},n_{k+2}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1107
research_problems.statement: Let $r \ge 2$. Is every large integer the sum of at most $r + 1$ many $r$-powerful numbers?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1081
research_problems.statement:
Let $A(x)$ count the number of $n\leq x$ which are the sum of two squarefull numbers (a number
$m$ is squarefull if $p\mid m$ implies $p^2\mid m$). Is it true that
$$A(x) \sim c \frac{x}{\sqrt{\log x}}$$
for some $c>0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #940
research_problems.statement:
Let $r \ge 3$. Is it true that the set of integers which are the sum of at most $r$ $r$-powerful numbers
has density $0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #322
research_problems.statement: Let $k\geq 3$ and $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ be the set of $k$th powers. What is the order of growth of $1_A^{(k)}(n)$, i.e. the number of representations of $n$ as the sum of $k$ many $k$th powers? Does there exist some $c>0$ and infinitely many $n$ such that $$1_A^{(k)}(n) >n^c?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #137
research_problems.statement:
We say that $N$ is powerful if whenever $p\mid N$ we also have $p^2\mid N$.

Let $k\geq 3$. Can the product of any $k$ consecutive positive integers ever be powerful?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #121
research_problems.statement:
Let $F_{k}(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that the product of no
$k$ many distinct elements of $A$ is a square. Is $F_5(N)=(1-o(1))N$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #364
research_problems.statement: There is no consecutive triple of powerful numbers.

title: Diophantine approximation and irrationality
summary: How well can a real number be approximated by $p/q$? Dirichlet gives $|\alpha - p/q| < 1/q^2$ infinitely often; Roth (1955) shows algebraic irrationals cannot do much better. Irrationality proofs (Apéry's $\zeta(3)$) are quantitative statements of this kind.
key_statements: \Big|\alpha-\frac pq\Big| < \frac{1}{q^{2+\varepsilon}} \ \text{has finitely many solutions for algebraic } \alpha \ \text{(Roth)}

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #267
research_problems.statement:
Let $F_1=F_2=1$ and $F_{n+1} = F_n + F_{n-1}$ be the Fibonacci sequence.
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an infinite sequence with $\frac{n_{k+1}}{n_k} \ge c > 1$. Must
$\sum_k \frac 1 {F_{n_k}}$ be irrational?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1147
research_problems.statement:
Let $\alpha>0$ be an irrational number. Is the set
$$A=\left\{ n\geq 1: \| \alpha n^2\| < \frac{1}{\log n}\right\},$$
where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the distance to the nearest integer, an additive basis of order $2$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1002
research_problems.statement:
For any $0<\alpha<1$, let $f(\alpha,n)=\frac{1}{\log n}\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}(\tfrac{1}{2}-
\{ \alpha k\})$. Does $f(\alpha,n)$ have an asymptotic distribution function?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #999
research_problems.statement:
For any function $f:\mathbb{N}\to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ the property that, for almost all
$\alpha$
$$\left\lvert \alpha-\frac{p}{q}\right\rvert < \frac{f(q)}{q}$$
has infinitely many solutions with $(p,q)=1$, is equivalent to
$$\sum_{q\geq 1}\phi(q)\frac{f(q)}{q}=\infty.$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #257
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set. Is
$$
\sum_{n\in A} \frac{1}{2^n - 1}
$$
irrational?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #252
research_problems.statement: Erdős Problem 252: irrationality of the sum for a given $k$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #260
research_problems.statement:
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be an increasing sequence such that $\frac{a_n}{n} \to \infty$.
Is the sum $\sum_{n}^{\infty} \frac{a_n}{2^{a_n}}$ irrational?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1049
research_problems.statement:
Let $t>1$ be a rational number. Is
$\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{1}{t^n-1}=\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\tau(n)}{t^n}$ irrational, where
$\tau(n)$ counts the divisors of $n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1051
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that if $a_0 < a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ is a strictly increasing sequence
of integers with $\liminf a_n^{1/2^n} > 1$, then the series
$\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{1}{a_n \cdot a_{n+1}}$ is irrational?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1050
research_problems.statement: The series $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{2^n - 3}$ is irrational.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #69
research_problems.statement:
Is
$$
\sum_{n\geq 2}\frac{\omega(n)}{2^n}
$$
irrational? (Here $\omega(n)$ counts the number of distinct prime divisors of $n$.)

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #495
research_problems.statement:
Let $\alpha,\beta \in \mathbb{R}$. Is it true that$$\liminf_{n\to \infty} n \| n\alpha \|
  \| n\beta\| =0$$? This is also known as the Littlewood conjecture.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #266
research_problems.statement:
Let $a_n$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converges.
There exists some integer $t \ge 1$ such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n + t}$ is irrational.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #264
research_problems.statement:
A sequence $a_n$ of integers is called an irrationality sequence if for every bounded sequence of integers $b_n$ with $a_n + b_n \neq 0$ and
$b_n \neq 0$ for all $n$, the sum
$$
  \sum \frac{1}{a_n + b_n}
$$
is irrational.

Note: there are other possible definitions of this concept. See
FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/263.lean for another possible definition.

(a) Is $2^n$ an example of an irrationality sequence? Kovač and Tao proved that it is not [KoTa24]

(b) Is $n!$ an example of an irrationality sequence?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #250
research_problems.statement:
Is
$$
  \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\sigma(n)}{2^n}
$$
irrational? Here $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of divisors function.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #258
research_problems.statement:
Let $a_n \to \infty$ be a sequence of non-zero natural numbers. Is
$\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{(a_1 ... a_n)}$ irrational, where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #247
research_problems.statement:
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \cdots$ be a sequence of integers such that
$$
  \limsup \frac{n_k}{k} = \infty.
$$
Is
$$
  \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2^{n_k}}
$$
transcendental?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #259
research_problems.statement: Is $\sum_{n} \mu(n)^2\frac{n}{2^n}$ irrational?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #249
research_problems.statement:
Is
$$\sum_{n} \frac{\phi(n)}{2^n}$$
irrational? Here $\phi$ is the Euler totient function.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #263
research_problems.statement:
(a) Is $a_n = 2^{2^n}$ an irrationality sequence in the above sense?

(b) Must every irrationality sequence $a_n$ in the above sense
satisfy $a_n^{1/n} \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #243
research_problems.statement:
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \dots$ be a sequence of integers such that
$\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{a_n}{a_{n-1}^2} = 1$ and $\sum \frac{1}{a_n} \in \mathbb{Q}$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1000
research_problems.statement:
Let $A=\{n_1<n_2<\cdots\}$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers, and let $\phi_A(k)$
count the number of $1\leq m\leq n_k$ such that the fraction $\frac{m}{n_k}$ cannot be written
as $\frac{b}{n_j}$ for any integer $b$ and any $j<k$; equivalently,
$$
\frac{n_k}{(m,n_k)}\nmid n_j
$$
for all $1\leq j<k$.

Is there a sequence $A$ such that
$$
\lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k\leq N}\frac{\phi_A(k)}{n_k}=0?
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #68
research_problems.statement:
Is
$$\sum_{n=2}^\infty \frac{1}{n!-1}$$
irrational?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #270
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$. Is it true that
$$\sum_{n\geq 1} \frac{1}{(n+1)\cdots (n+f(n))}$$
is irrational?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #251
research_problems.statement: Is $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{p_n}{2^n}$ irrational? Here $p_n$ is the $n$-th prime ($p_1=2, p_2=3, \dots$).
